summary: Submitted draft/submission.json (action=research) refreshing the implementation map after the fourth obligation was answered in scope, with draft/map-v4.json as the new base (base version 3). The refresh clears the two fact-level unknowns that were answered by the confirmed checks — whether the heartbeat callback can publish a term lower than one the main goroutine already adopted, and whether the vote-record overwrite can be combined with the transfer exemption and an abstaining voter to produce two leaders in one term — and leaves the mechanism that answered each one in the behavior that owns it, so the frontier no longer advertises answered questions. The candidate behavior now records the exemption in its campaign branch (the transfer path keeps pre-vote from filtering the campaign, so a published term that has dropped below a recorded vote's term lets the campaign propose it, overwrite the record and collect a quorum while another voter's record is still empty) and narrows its remaining question to whether that dual leadership can be made to persist and whether two leaders of one term can commit conflicting entries. The core overview rationale names the third mechanism, explains its link to the first (the overwritten record is the only barrier the vote path's exemption leaves) and keeps the counter-parts that bound all three, so the status stays usable and no core gap is claimed. The submission carries four clarification map_changes and states explicitly that no requirement, identity, context or fact edge changed: the facts keep their assertions, identity, validity context, representation, durability, recovery and edges, and the behavior keeps its owner, trigger, guards and fact edges. One mechanical hurdle is worth noting: reproducing the map's long single-line objects through the patch tool failed to match, and the update was applied as a mechanical JSON field rewrite before validation, which succeeded and was then checked by the trusted validator. The run's frontier now shows, on one side, four confirmed in-scope results (the term regression, the unanswered client futures on a shut-down node, the local vote-once violation and the two-leader overlap) and, on the other, the leads that remain genuinely open: the production-TCP scheduling question on the heartbeat entry point, the enqueue-before-shutdown question and repair choice on the client futures, the configuration-change/matching question on the follower match index, and the two deferred surfaces (the configuration future's zero index and the commit context a follower leaves after installing a snapshot). Optional preflight with the trusted validator returned valid=true; no target code was executed for this product.
